ig_caption:
The Scotch Game starts 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4: White doesn't wait, and opens the centre at once. Here it is at three levels.

At 800: after 3...exd4 4.Nxd4 White's knight sits in the middle and White keeps a pawn on e4. Now bring the rest of your pieces out quickly.
At 1200: in the Classical, 4...Bc5, Black aims three pieces at the d4 knight. Count attackers and defenders: Be3 and c3 keep it safe.
At 1600: in the Mieses line, 4...Nf6, both queens end up in front of their own bishops, and 8.c4 chases Black's knight.

The name comes from a match played by letter between Edinburgh and London that began in 1824.

Do you play 3.d4 or 3.Bc4? 👇

slides.title: At 800: the idea
slides.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4
slides.take: White doesn't wait. 3.d4 hits e5 at once, and after the swap the knight sits in the middle of the board.
slides.edge: White keeps a pawn on e4 and Black has none in the centre. Now bring your other pieces out fast.

slides.title: At 1200: the Classical
slides.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Bc5 Be3 Qf6 c3 Nge7
slides.take: Black aims three pieces at the d4 knight: the knight on c6, the bishop on c5 and the queen on f6.
slides.edge: Count attackers and defenders. With Be3 and c3, White has enough, and can then bring out the bishop to c4.

slides.title: At 1600: the Mieses
slides.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nxc6 bxc6 e5 Qe7 Qe2 Nd5 c4
slides.take: After 6.e5 Qe7 7.Qe2, both queens stand in front of their own bishops on f1 and f8.
slides.edge: Then 8.c4 chases the knight away. It looks strange, but strong players still argue over it.

slides.title: Why is it called Scotch?
slides.body: The name comes from a match played by letter between Edinburgh and London, which began in 1824.
slides.note: Kasparov brought it back to the top in 1990, in his world title match against Karpov.
